prompt: Keep both people, their clothing and the kitchen exactly as in the reference image. A father steadies a child's hands around a wooden spoon, then lets go; the child stirs once, too fast, sauce flicks onto the counter, and both freeze and look at each other. The camera sits low at counter height, static with a tiny drift right. Warm late-afternoon light from a side window, steam rising. Flour dust, dented pan, tea towel. Simmering pot and a spoon tapped on enamel.
title: Teaching a Child to Cook
summary: A father lets go of the spoon, the child stirs too fast, and both freeze.
why: The beat is a small failure followed by shared laughter, and both halves are physical: a hand released, one stir too fast, a shared freeze. That is a performance a model can hold because nothing depends on facial nuance. A nearly static camera at counter height keeps attention on the hands, and image-to-video is used so the two characters and the kitchen stay consistent across the whole take.
reference_note: Upload a two-character still with an adult and a child together at a counter or table, both at similar distance from camera and lit by window light. Avoid images where the child's face is turned away or hidden, and avoid stock-photo gloss — the model keeps that polish and it flattens the moment.
